opening.lessonTitle: This week I’m working in Porto
questions: Where do you work or study?
opening.alternativeIfNeither: Do you have English classes at home?

use.label: This week

affirmative.oralPrompt: Imagine Ana’s week. Say one thing she usually does and one thing she’s doing this week.

questions.negativeStructure: Subject + am / is / are + not + verb-ing
negativeExamples: I’m not working now. I’m studying.

dialogue.instruction: Read the conversation with your teacher.

dialogue.speaker: Ana
dialogue.text: Hi, Kim! I’m in Porto. I’m working here this week.

dialogue.speaker: Kim
dialogue.text: Do you usually work in Porto?

dialogue.speaker: Ana
dialogue.text: No, I don’t. I usually work from home.

dialogue.speaker: Ana
dialogue.text: I’m drinking coffee next to the river. I have a meeting at ten.

dialogue.speaker: Ana
dialogue.text: Sorry? Can you say that again? Kim? Kim?

comprehension.a: She’s drinking coffee next to the river.

personal.instruction: Compare your usual evenings with this week. Then find one similarity with your teacher.
questions: What do you usually do in the evening?
Ask your teacher about her evenings. Find one thing you have in common.
personal.alternativeIfNeither: Do you usually have English classes at home?

listening.instruction: Listen to Kim. Answer, then reply.

questions.q: Is Kim walking in the park?
questions.fullAnswer: Yes, she is. She’s walking in the park.

questions.q: Does Kim usually work in the morning?
questions.fullAnswer: Yes, she does. She usually works in the morning.

questions.q: Is Kim working in the morning this week?
questions.fullAnswer: No, she isn’t. She’s working in the evening.

listening.replyPrompt: Kim is working in the evening this week. Tell her when you’re free for a call.
optionalSupport: I’m free in the morning / afternoon / evening.
listening.transcript: Hi, Ana! Sorry, bad signal! Never mind. I’m walking in the park next to my home. I usually work in the morning, but this week I’m working in the evening. Maybe I can travel to Porto soon! See you on Monday!

roleplay.situation: Your teacher is Kim. Call her and find out about her day.
steps: Find out where Kim is and what she is doing.
Ask about her usual routine and this week.
Ask her to repeat when the signal is bad.
Swap roles. Answer about your life or choose a situation.
optionalSupport: Sorry? Can you say that again?
